text:
Alex Chen: quick sync — we're seeing traces drop when gateway batches requests into our worker queue. traceparent exists on http, but consumer spans come back as new roots. anyone seen this?
Maria Gomez: yup saw similar in staging yesterday. looks like SQS message attributes got trimmed by the batcher.
Tyler Patel: do we add trace headers to the batch envelope or per-message attrs? current gateway puts headers into the envelope only.
Alex Chen: envelope-only was our first pass to avoid per-message overhead. problem is downstream consumers read per-message attrs.
Jess Rivera: envelope semantics are fragile for retries and partial failures. if a single message is retried the envelope context can be lost or repurposed.
Samir Iqbal: we also re-order messages when we micro-batch for throughput, which can break span parent/child assumptions. recommendation: either attach traceparent to each message or use span linking on consume.
Maria Gomez: +1 for per-message traceparent. storage cost is tiny and decoding is cheap. Also we need to propagate baggage for tenant ids (but we should redact PII).
Alex Chen: what about using span.Link instead of parent to avoid reparenting? consumer could start a new root and link to original span ids.
Tyler Patel: linking avoids reparenting but makes waterfall traces harder to read in timeline view. our dashboard traces viewer currently expects parent->child relationships for latency breakdowns.
Jess Rivera: visualizations aside, linking is safer semantically for async. we should keep both options available and choose by route policy.
Samir Iqbal: practical snippet for producer — attach as message attrs:
```
MessageAttributes:{
  traceparent: { DataType: 'String', StringValue: traceparent },
  tracestate: { DataType: 'String', StringValue: tracestate },
  ot_baggage: { DataType: 'String', StringValue: base64(baggage_json) }
}
```
Alex Chen: consumer rehydrate example:
```py
# pseudo
attrs = msg.MessageAttributes or {}
tp = attrs.get('traceparent')
if tp:
    ctx = propagator.extract({'traceparent': tp, 'tracestate': attrs.get('tracestate')})
    with tracer.start_as_current_span('worker.process', context=ctx):
        process(msg)
else:
    # fallback: link original ids if available
    links = []
    if attrs.get('orig-span-id'):
        links = [SpanLink(trace_id=attrs['orig-trace-id'], span_id=attrs['orig-span-id'])]
    with tracer.start_as_current_span('worker.process', links=links):
        process(msg)
```
Maria Gomez: note: some infra (SNS->SQS subscription) base64-encodes attributes. we need canonicalize step at gateway: normalize header key names (lowercase), base64 decode, validate W3C traceparent format.
Tyler Patel: and watch sampling: if gateway samples out (drop spans), we still want items to flow with traceparent so downstream can decide. we should not mutate sampled flag in headers unless policy requires it.
Jess Rivera: retention/exporter note — when we reparent or link a lot, ingest volume spikes. ingest-bot has been dropping spans when our OTLP pipeline hits retention thresholds.
ingest-bot: warning: OTLP exporter queue > 90% (last 5m). oldest-span-age=12m. consider batching/adjust sampling or increasing retention.
Samir Iqbal: for high-throughput routes we should enable tail-based sampling at collector with policy keyed by route and env, and keep header propagation intact.
Alex Chen: action items: 1) gateway: write per-message trace attrs + canonicalizer 2) consumer libs: provide rehydrate helper + optional link helper 3) dashboard: add link visualization toggle and mark linked spans so UX doesn't mislead 4) infra: adjust OTLP retention for bursty routes.
Maria Gomez: I'll open a PR with a tiny canonicalizer util (lowercase keys, decode base64, validate traceparent regex).
Tyler Patel: I'll prototype a small change in the gateway to attach per-message attrs when batch_size <= 50 and fall back to envelope for massive fanout but still include mapping of message_index->traceparent in envelope.
Jess Rivera: document privacy: baggage keys must be whitelisted. don't allow freeform user baggage into exporters.
Samir Iqbal: +1. also add tests for retry semantics — message gets retried, consumer should rehydrate same context regardless of ordering.
Alex Chen: awesome. can we target a canary this week for low-volume routes? keep me posted.
Maria Gomez: will do, PR by EOD.
Tyler Patel: will add unit tests.
Jess Rivera: I'll update the rollout checklist to include ingress tagging and observe ingest-bot metrics.
Samir Iqbal: thanks — logging snippets in PR will help debug.
Alex Chen: :thumbsup:
